title_en: The Fast Life Collection Honors the Legendary Cars of The Fast and the Furious With an Exclusive New Die-Cast Car Drop
summary_en: We've got an exclusive first look at Jada Toys' Fast Life collection, which celebrates the iconic cars of The Fast and the Furious franchise.
body_en:
Universal Pictures is kicking off a new merchandising brand aimed at celebrating the iconic cars of The Fast and The Furious franchise. It's dubbed Fast Life, and IGN has an exclusive first look at what Jada Toys is bringing to the table.
Jada Toys' Fast Life line kicks off with two versions of the Nissan Skyline GT-R driven by the late Paul Walker's character Brian O'Conner. The first is based on the car's appearance in 2003's 2 Fast 2 Furious. The second features a unique reverse livery design aimed at showcasing the Fast Life line's emphasis on customization and expression.
Check out the slideshow gallery below for an early look at both versions of the collectible car:
These cars are 1:24 scale die-cast replicas. They're priced at $59.99 each.
Jada Toys will be showing off both toys at the 2026 SEMA Show from November 3–6, at West Hall at Booth #54233.
“SEMA is the perfect place to introduce Jada’s line of collectibles inspired by Universal’s new Fast Life brand because it brings together the cars, creators, brands, and enthusiasts who shape car culture,” said Jada's CEO Bill Simons in a statement. “We’re building on Jada’s legacy in die-cast and licensed collectibles to create something that connects the real-world automotive scene with the films and vehicles fans have grown up with. Bringing the Liberty Walk GT-R to SEMA alongside Brian’s Skyline makes this an exciting first look at the collection.”
Preorders for both cars are now open on the Jada Toys website. You can find individual links below:
In other Fast and Furious news, the next film in the series finally has a title and a release date . It's expected that Fast Forever will be the final film in the long-running franchise , though a Peacock series is now also in the works .
